key_insight: VisDom improves sparse novel view synthesis by adding a "visible domain" constraint, helping models focus on geometry that is actually supported by the input views. This reduces overfitting, floating artifacts, and inconsistent 3D reconstructions in sparse-view settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of recovering accurate 3D geometry and realistic novel views from only a few input images, where NeRF- and Gaussian Splatting-based methods often overfit and produce artifacts. It also tackles the limitation of silhouette-only regularization, which can include regions outside the true object shape.
method: Introduces a visible domain constraint to restrict learning to regions that are truly supported by the observed views.
Uses this constraint as a regularizer for sparse-view novel view synthesis to improve geometric consistency.
Builds on NeRF/GS-style pipelines while reducing hallucinated or floating content in unobserved areas.
impact: For practitioners, VisDom offers a practical way to make sparse-view reconstruction more reliable without requiring dense supervision. This can improve results in 3D capture, robotics, AR/VR, and other applications where collecting many views is difficult.
